name: Chang'e 7
short_status: Launch postponed: on 23 Aug 2026 the China Manned Space Engineering Office said Chang'e 7 does not meet the conditions for launch and cannot fly in this year's scheduled window. No Chinese official source has given a new date or a reason; partner agencies say 2027 (as of 2 Nov 2026).
tagline: CNSA · China · Lander · 2027 · Commercial and multipolar In development
stats: launch mass of the four-spacecraft stack
candidate-site latitude shown by CNSA (not final), closer to a pole than any landing so far
science payloads, six of them international
spacecraft in one mission: orbiter, lander, rover, hopper

facts.label: Rollout (19 Aug 2026)
facts.value: The Chang'e 7 probe and its Long March 5 Y14 finished work in the technical area at Wenchang and the combined stack was moved upright to the launch area. The China Manned Space Engineering Office (CMSE) said launch was planned 计划近日择机实施发射, at an opportune time in the coming days; CNSA reposted the notice.

facts.label: Launch postponed (23 Aug 2026)
facts.value: CMSE: 本着稳妥可靠、万无一失的原则，经综合研判，嫦娥七号任务不满足发射条件，不能在今年预定窗口实施 (in keeping with the principle of being steady and reliable and leaving nothing to chance, and after a comprehensive assessment, the Chang'e 7 mission does not meet the conditions for launch and cannot be carried out in this year's scheduled window). No reason, new date or year was given. Xinhua carried the notice at 20:01 Beijing time.

facts.label: New launch timing (partner statements)
facts.value: Thailand's NARIT said on 24 Aug 2026 that the launch moves to 2027, because Tropical Storm Narra led to cancelling the launch planned for 24 August and no period with favorable sunlight at the landing site remains in 2026. ILOA's ILO-C page said on 14 Sep 2026 that launch is now scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Neither is a Chinese announcement.

facts.label: Rollback (reported)
facts.value: China in Space reported that the stack was rolled back from the pad to the assembly building on 24 Aug 2026, in clear weather. No Chinese official or state media report of the rollback has been found.

facts.label: Status (as of 2 Nov 2026)
facts.value: Not launched. No Chinese official source (CMSE, CNSA or CLEP) has named a new launch date, year or reason since the 23 August notice, and no Xinhua or China News Service report of one has been found. On 31 Oct 2026 CCTV, reporting from CMSE's crewed spaceflight academic conference, listed Chang'e 7 among missions the program will complete as planned, with no date.

facts.label: Earlier official window (superseded)
facts.value: Second half of 2026, announced by the China Manned Space Engineering Office on 10 Apr 2026 and replaced by the postponement notice of 23 Aug 2026

facts.label: Spacecraft arrived at Wenchang
facts.value: 9 April 2026, flown to Hainan ahead of pre-launch testing

facts.label: Rocket delivered
facts.value: Long March 5 arrived by sea at Wenchang 12-13 July 2026 (12th Long March 5 flight)

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Orbiter + lander + rover + rocket-powered hopping probe, about 8,200 kg at launch

facts.label: Landing target
facts.value: CNSA has published no final landing site. Officially the target is the illuminated terrain near Shackleton crater in the south polar region, with a landing accuracy goal better than 100 m. The widely repeated figure of 88.8 S / 123.4 E (with other candidates near Shoemaker and Haworth) is the candidate site highlighted on a map in a February 2025 presentation by CNSA's Lunar Exploration and Space Engineering Center to the UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space; no final site has been announced

facts.label: Mission profile
facts.value: About 90 days in lunar polar orbit surveying the site before a landing attempt (plan published before the delay; no new dates)

facts.label: Payloads
facts.value: 21 science payloads cited by Chinese media, including 6 international (Egypt/Bahrain, Switzerland, Thailand, Italy, Russia, ILOA's ILO-C telescope)

facts.label: Hopper
facts.value: Legged, rocket-propelled probe carrying the LUWA water-molecule analyzer; designed for repeated flights into permanently shadowed craters

facts.label: Relay
facts.value: Queqiao-2 relay satellite (launched 20 March 2024), which also carries three mission payloads

facts.label: Science goal
facts.value: First direct on-surface detection and analysis of water ice at the lunar south pole; site survey for the ILRS

facts.label: Not the rocket that failed in August 2026
facts.value: A Long March 7A carrying the ChinaSat-4B communications satellite failed shortly after lifting off from Wenchang on 10 Aug 2026. That was a different vehicle, a different payload and a different pad (LC-201; the Long March 5 flies from LC-101). The 23 August notice postponing Chang'e 7 gave no reason, and no official source has linked the two. No cause for the failure has been attributed.

facts.label: Engine commonality (analyst context only)
facts.value: Analysts note the Long March 7A's first stage and boosters use YF-100 engines, the same type used on the Long March 5's boosters, so an engine-related cause could in principle touch other vehicles. This is analyst observation with no official statement behind it, and no fleet stand-down has been announced.
